data.name: ObjectMatchingSwitchToAdvanced
data.value: The proposal switches this Connected System to Advanced matching, so the rules held against each Connected System Object Type stop being used and each Synchronization Rule's own rules apply instead. A Synchronization Rule carrying no rules of its own joins nothing.

data.name: ObjectMatchingSwitchToSimple
data.value: The proposal switches this Connected System to Simple matching, so each Synchronization Rule's own rules stop being used and the rules held against each Connected System Object Type apply instead. An Object Type carrying no rules of its own joins nothing.

data.name: ObjectMatchingOwnerSyncRule
data.value: a Synchronization Rule

data.name: ObjectMatchingNoMetaverseObjectType
data.value: {0} names no Metaverse Object Type to search. Simple mode rules must name one; in Advanced mode the Synchronization Rule supplies it.

data.name: BehaviourSameSettings
data.value: The proposed settings match the ones this Synchronization Rule already has, so nothing would change and no impact is counted below.

data.name: BehaviourDirectionImmutable
data.value: Direction cannot be changed on a saved Synchronization Rule. This rule's Attribute Flow mappings and Object Matching Rules are written for {0}, and would all address the wrong side as {1}. Create a rule in the direction you need instead.

data.name: BehaviourEnabling
data.value: Enabling this Synchronization Rule starts it contributing on the next synchronization: it begins flowing its Attribute Flow mappings, and whatever it projects or provisions starts being created.

data.name: BehaviourDisabling
data.value: Disabling this Synchronization Rule stops it contributing on the next synchronization. Attribute values it currently owns pass to another contributor where there is one, and are kept, ready for the rule to be enabled again, where it was the only one. It stops projecting and provisioning.

data.name: BehaviourRuleDisabled
data.value: This Synchronization Rule is disabled, so no synchronization applies it today. The impact below describes what the next synchronization would do once it is enabled.

data.name: DestructiveOutboundOnExport
data.value: The Outbound Deprovision Action is read only by export Synchronization Rules, so changing it on this import rule changes no object's fate and is not counted below.

data.name: DestructiveInboundOnImport
data.value: The Inbound Out-of-Scope Action is read only by import Synchronization Rules, so changing it on this export rule changes no object's fate and is not counted below.

data.name: DestructiveRuleDisabled
data.value: This Synchronization Rule is disabled, so no synchronization applies its settings today. The counts below describe what the next synchronization would do once it is enabled.

data.name: DestructiveSiblingKeepsJoin
data.value: {0} also covers this object type and keeps its objects joined (Remain Joined). Where an object leaves every import Synchronization Rule, the rules that held it decide, and Remain Joined from any of them keeps the join, so this change disconnects only objects those rules never held. The counts below include only those.

data.name: DeletionSettingsNeedsAuthoritativeSource
data.value: Deleting when an authoritative source disconnects needs at least one Connected System named as an authoritative source. Without one, synchronization falls back to deleting when the last connector disconnects, which is a different rule from the one selected.

data.name: ScopingProposalSameAsStored
data.value: The proposed Scoping Criteria match the ones this Synchronization Rule already has, so no object changes scope and no impact is counted below.

data.name: ScopingProposalRemovesEveryCriterion
data.value: The proposal removes every Scoping Criterion, so this Synchronization Rule would manage every object of type '{0}' rather than a selected population.

data.name: ScopingProposalRuleDisabled
data.value: This Synchronization Rule is disabled, so no synchronization applies its scope today. The counts below describe what the next synchronization would do once it is enabled.

data.name: ScopingProposalUnscopedSiblingDisconnect
data.value: Import Synchronization Rule '{0}' covers this object type with no Scoping Criteria, so every object stays joined whatever this rule says: narrowing this rule's criteria disconnects nothing. An object that leaves this rule's scope stops receiving its Attribute Flow; under its Out-of-Scope Action, Disconnect, the values this rule contributed are handed to the rules that still cover the object.

data.name: ScopingProposalUnscopedSiblingRemainJoined
data.value: Import Synchronization Rule '{0}' covers this object type with no Scoping Criteria, so every object stays joined whatever this rule says: narrowing this rule's criteria disconnects nothing. An object that leaves this rule's scope stops receiving its Attribute Flow; under its Out-of-Scope Action, Remain Joined, the values this rule contributed stay as they are.

data.name: ScopingProposalExpressionReadsMetaverseOnImport
data.value: A proposed Scoping Criterion's expression reads {0}, but an import Synchronization Rule evaluates its scope against Connected System attributes (cs["..."]), so that input would never hold a value.

data.name: ScopingProposalExpressionReadsConnectedSystemOnExport
data.value: A proposed Scoping Criterion's expression reads {0}, but an export Synchronization Rule evaluates its scope against Metaverse Attributes (mv["..."]), so that input would never hold a value.

data.name: ScopingProposalReadsMetaverseOnImport
data.value: A proposed Scoping Criterion reads a Metaverse Attribute, but an import Synchronization Rule evaluates its scope against Connected System attributes, so the criterion would never match and the scope would be wider than it appears.

data.name: ScopingProposalReadsConnectedSystemOnExport
data.value: A proposed Scoping Criterion reads a Connected System attribute, but an export Synchronization Rule evaluates its scope against Metaverse Attributes, so the criterion would never match and the scope would be wider than it appears.

data.name: AttributeFlowSameAsStored
data.value: The proposed Attribute Flow matches the mappings this Synchronization Rule already has, so no object changes and no impact is counted below.

data.name: AttributeFlowRemovesEveryMapping
data.value: The proposal removes every mapping, so this Synchronization Rule would flow nothing.

data.name: AttributeFlowRuleDisabled
data.value: This Synchronization Rule is disabled, so no synchronization applies its Attribute Flow today. The values below describe what the next synchronization would write once it is enabled.

data.name: AttributeFlowRemovedKeepValues
data.value: The proposal removes this Synchronization Rule's Attribute Flow to '{0}', and you chose to keep the values it contributed. They remain in place with no record of where they came from, and no synchronization will ever recall them; no value change is counted below for them.

data.name: AttributeFlowRemovedRecalled
data.value: The proposal removes this Synchronization Rule's Attribute Flow to '{0}'. The values it contributed are recalled at the next synchronization of the contributing Connected System, Delta or Full: where another Attribute Flow also contributes the attribute its value takes over, otherwise the attribute is cleared. No value change is counted below for them, because the recall happens in that synchronization rather than in this save.

data.name: AttributeFlowBelowPriority
data.value: The proposed mapping for '{0}' sits below {1} in Attribute Priority, so a synchronization would evaluate it and then write nothing. Raise its priority to make it the contributor that wins the attribute.

data.name: AttributeFlowDependantMissingInput
data.value: Once this proposal is saved, the Attribute Flow to '{0}' on Synchronization Rule '{1}' would be missing an input: it reads {2}. Its Missing Input Behavior then decides what it writes.

data.name: AttributeFlowOtherSystemReader
data.value: The Attribute Flow to '{0}' on Synchronization Rule '{1}' {2}, which this proposal changes. It runs in that Synchronization Rule's own Connected System, so it is re-evaluated when that Connected System next synchronizes; what it would write is not counted below.

data.name: AttributeFlowWritesConnectedSystemOnImport
data.value: A proposed Attribute Flow mapping writes a Connected System attribute, but an import Synchronization Rule flows into the Metaverse, so the mapping would write nothing.

data.name: AttributeFlowWritesMetaverseOnExport
data.value: A proposed Attribute Flow mapping writes a Metaverse Attribute, but an export Synchronization Rule flows out to a Connected System, so the mapping would write nothing.

data.name: SchemaDeselectingObjectType
data.value: Deselecting {0} takes its objects out of management. The next Full Import no longer returns them, so the objects already imported become obsolete, and the following synchronization disconnects them from their Metaverse Objects, which may leave those eligible for deletion. The Run Profile's deletion limits apply to them as to any other deleted object.

data.name: SchemaOverlapDeselectFallsToOther
data.value: Deselecting {0} does not take its objects that also carry {1} out of management: with {0} deselected, those entries resolve to {1}, so the import returns them as {1} objects rather than as the {0} objects JIM holds. By default each import refuses them, reports each as an Object Type Changed error and keeps it as {0} rather than obsoleting it, so the number of objects described as becoming obsolete overstates what happens to them. If the intent is to stop managing those objects, scope them out by container or partition instead, because deselecting {0} changes their Object Type rather than removing them. If they should become {1} objects, run a Full Import with Allow Object Type Changes enabled on its Run Profile: JIM retires the {0} objects and imports them as new {1} objects, in scope of the Synchronization Rules for {1}.

data.name: SchemaMoveInstruction
data.value: To move them, run a Full Import with Allow Object Type Changes enabled on its Run Profile: JIM retires the {0} objects and imports them as new {1} objects, so a Synchronization Rule for {1} needs to be ready to join them to the same Metaverse Objects.
